carbon-black.purpose: The chassis: page ground, and the text colour on top of either accent.

panel-carbon.purpose: Every lifted surface, exactly one tonal step above the ground.

charcoal.purpose: Borders and dividers ONLY. Never a text colour.

papaya-whip.purpose: Primary content: full-emphasis text and the resting colour of every Morse bar.

muted-charcoal.purpose: Secondary text: prose, labels, counts, inactive controls.

bubblegum-tint.purpose: Transmission. Sounding bar, Play, oscilloscope trace, selected filter.

cool-sky.purpose: State and interaction. Active tab, eyebrow labels, caret, focus rings.

on-accent.purpose: Text and icons placed on top of pink or blue.

display.purpose: The plain-text editor while it holds primacy; drops to 24px when Morse leads.

title.purpose: The current word above the rhythm strip; positive tracking separates characters to match the bars.

body.purpose: All prose, set in Muted Charcoal, capped at a 596px measure (~68 characters).

label.purpose: Mono eyebrows, transport captions, chart filters and readouts.

code.purpose: The Morse editor. Wider tracking because gaps between groups carry meaning.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: System default. Depth is tonal layering plus one hairline border, never a drop shadow.

shadows.name: floating-banner
shadows.purpose: The single documented exception: the consent banner, which genuinely floats over the page.

shadows.name: bar-bloom-outer
shadows.purpose: The sounding bar glow. A readout, not a material — only ever on a bar that is playing right now.

shadows.name: bar-bloom-inner
shadows.purpose: Inner core of the sounding bar bloom.

shadows.name: strip-bloom
shadows.purpose: Faint pink wash behind the rhythm strip; the only ambient glow in the system.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: Free Mode key pad while held. The one glow that is not pink.

motion.name: ease-instrument
motion.purpose: The nav pill slide (380ms) and the consent banner entrance (260ms). Decisive, no overshoot.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Hover and press feedback on chart cells, transport and icon buttons.

motion.name: state-slow
motion.purpose: Nav tab colour change, slower than the pill it sits under so the fill leads.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global prefers-reduced-motion override on all animation, transition and scroll-behavior.

morseGeometry.name: --diagram-unit

morseGeometry.purpose: Content column width, measured at ~68 characters per line.

components.name: Rhythm Strip Bars
components.description: The signature: width equals duration. Dit 1 unit, dah 3 units, gaps 1/3/7. The third bar is sounding.

narrative.overview:
Morsia is drawn as a piece of lab equipment, not as a web page. The reference is a signal generator or a bench oscilloscope: a dark chassis, panels milled into it, a readout that is the point of the object, and a small number of coloured indicators that mean something specific. Nothing here is decorative. Every colour, every glow and every label is reporting a state.

This matters because the product's whole claim is that Morse is time, not notation. Every character is drawn as proportional bars whose on-screen width equals their duration. A dah is exactly three times the width of a dit, because it is exactly three times as long. The gaps are drawn to scale too, so a seven-unit word gap is visibly seven units of silence. The interface is a measuring instrument pointed at a rhythm, and it earns the instrument look by actually being one.

The system is flat and dark. Depth comes from tonal layering — a lighter panel lifted off a darker ground by one hairline border — never from drop shadows. The one exception is glow, which is not decoration but the readout: a bar blooms pink at the exact moment it is sounding. Type is quiet and functional, with monospace reserved for anything the machine is reporting and a humanist sans for anything a person wrote.
keyCharacteristics: Width equals duration, everywhere, without exception
Dark chassis, lifted panels, hairline borders, no drop shadows
Two accent colours with strictly separated jobs, never on the same element
Monospace eyebrow labels with a leading dot, letterspaced and small
Generous corner radii (20-24px) on panels, full pills on controls
Glow used only as a live state readout, and only in pink

rules.name: The Separation Rule
rules.body: Pink and blue never appear on the same element. Pink is transmission; blue is state and interaction. An element that is both sounding and selected resolves to pink, because what it is doing outranks where it is.

rules.name: The Line-Colour Rule
rules.body: Charcoal (#575761) draws lines and nothing else. Muted text is Muted Charcoal (#9A9AA4), a full step lighter. Setting text in the border colour is the fastest way to make this interface look broken.

rules.name: The Channel Rule
rules.body: Every translucent value derives from a --*-rgb channel triple of a palette colour. No alpha variant is ever hand-mixed, so re-tinting the palette re-tints every derived line, fill and glow with it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo for what a human wrote, IBM Plex Mono for what the machine reports. A monospace label on human content, or a sans label on a readout, breaks the instrument fiction.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every panel is introduced by a 5px Cool Sky dot followed by a mono, 700-weight, 0.2em-tracked uppercase label in the same blue. The dot is aria-hidden; it is punctuation, not content.

rules.name: The Tracking-Is-Timing Rule
rules.body: Letterspacing is positive and generous on anything representing Morse or a machine state (0.06em to 0.2em) and negative on human display type (-0.015em to -0.03em). Tight type is a person talking; loose type is a signal.

rules.name: The Integer-Unit Rule
rules.body: Anything representing Morse is an exact multiple of its unit token. Never a fraction, never an eyeballed value. Width is duration, so an arbitrary width is a lie about time.

rules.name: The Glow-Means-Live Rule
rules.body: Glow appears only where something is happening right now, and outside Free Mode lamp it is always pink. A glow on a resting element is a false reading.

rules.name: The Flat-Chassis Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Lift comes from one tonal step plus one hairline border. Reach for a shadow and you have left the instrument.

rules.name: The Pill-Or-Panel Rule
rules.body: Interactive controls are pills (999px). Content containers are 20-24px panels. A 999px content card or a 20px nav tab reads as a mistake in this system.

dos: Do derive every Morse dimension from its unit token — --unit (22px) on the strip, --chart-bar-unit (6px) on the chart, --diagram-unit (10px) in diagrams — as exact integer multiples.
Do introduce every panel with the eyebrow: 5px Cool Sky dot, 9px gap, mono 12px 700 0.2em uppercase Cool Sky label.
Do set human-written content in Archivo and machine-reported content in IBM Plex Mono.
Do build translucency from the --*-rgb channel triples so alpha variants stay tied to the palette.
Do lift surfaces with one tonal step plus one 1px hairline border.
Do reserve Bubblegum Tint for transmission and Cool Sky for state, interaction and focus.
Do read canvas tokens once per mount/resize via readTokens().
Do keep the content column at --measure (596px) and identical across breakpoints.
donts: Don't set text in Charcoal (#575761). It is a line colour. Muted text is #9A9AA4.
Don't put pink and blue on the same element.
Don't add drop shadows. The consent banner is the one documented exception.
Don't glow anything that is not live right now.
Don't use pure black or pure white — the ground is warm-tinted carbon and the ink is Papaya Whip.
Don't draw a Morse element at an arbitrary width. Width is duration; an eyeballed width is a false reading.
Don't add a focus ring to the editors — the Cool Sky caret is the indicator, by owner's decision.
Don't let the four nav pills wrap; the rail scrolls instead.
Don't introduce a third accent colour. Two accents with separated jobs is the system.
